summary.title: Bempedoic acid at a glance
points: An ACL inhibitor: blocks cholesterol synthesis one step before statins; a prodrug activated in the liver.
Nilemdo (alone) and Nustendi (with ezetimibe), both Daiichi Sankyo Europe; one tablet a day.
Two indications: high cholesterol (with a statin, or without one if not possible) and CV risk reduction.
LDL −15–17% on a statin, −23–24% without; CLEAR Outcomes MACE 11.7% vs 13.3% (HR 0.87).
Watch uric acid and gout, small haemoglobin dips, creatinine rise, statin levels, pregnancy.

exercises.scenario: A patient who tolerates atorvastatin 80 mg well asks to switch to bempedoic acid instead.

questions.prompt: Does the label support replacing the statin?
options: Yes: it's an equal alternative to any statin
No: there's no route for patients who can take a statin
Yes, if LDL is already at goal on the statin and he prefers fewer side effects
Only as Nustendi, which includes ezetimibe
questions.explanation: It's added to the maximum tolerated statin, or used without one only if a statin can't be taken.

questions.prompt: What did CLEAR Outcomes reduce?
options: Deaths from any cause by about 13% overall
Cardiovascular deaths and strokes, not heart attacks
LDL only; it didn't measure clinical events
questions.explanation: Stroke and CV death didn't change significantly.

exercises.scenario: Why does creatinine rise on bempedoic acid?

questions.prompt: Choose the mechanism.
options: It breaks down into creatinine in the liver
It damages the kidney's filtering units over time
It blocks OAT2 in the kidney
It causes dehydration through extra urine
questions.explanation: The same transporter explains the uric acid rise.

questions.prompt: Which statin dose is contraindicated with it?
options: Rosuvastatin above 20 mg in Asian patients
Pravastatin at any dose, because of OATP
questions.explanation: Bempedoic acid roughly doubles simvastatin acid levels.

summary.title: How it works
points: Blocks ATP citrate lyase upstream of HMG-CoA reductase; the liver adds LDL receptors.
Activated by ACSVL1, mainly in the liver; the SmPC makes no muscle-benefit claim.
Also lowers apoB, non-HDL and CRP; HbA1c slightly lower in diabetes.
Cleared by glucuronidation (UGT2B7); no CYP effects; half-life about 19 hours.
Weak OATP1B1/1B3 blocking raises statins; OAT2 blocking raises creatinine and uric acid.

exercises.scenario: A patient on simvastatin 20 mg starts bempedoic acid.

questions.prompt: What happens to simvastatin acid levels?
options: They rise tenfold, so simvastatin must stop
They don't change, because CYP isn't involved
They fall by about half through UGT2B7
questions.explanation: Weak OATP1B1/1B3 blocking.

questions.prompt: What should be monitored?
options: Uric acid only, since the statin isn't affected
Blood sugar, because statins and bempedoic acid both raise it
Kidney function weekly for the first month
Statin side effects, especially muscle symptoms
questions.explanation: Higher statin exposure raises muscle risk.

exercises.scenario: A colleague says bempedoic acid 'avoids muscle pain because it isn't active in muscle'.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC actually say?
options: Only that ACSVL1 is mainly in the liver
That it causes no muscle side effects at all
That it's contraindicated in muscle disease
That it's proven safer for muscles than statins
questions.explanation: No muscle-benefit claim is made.

questions.prompt: Why is the LDL effect smaller on top of a statin?
options: The dose is lower when combined with a statin
Statins block the activation of bempedoic acid in the liver
The statin already acts on the same pathway
Statins speed up its clearance via CYP3A4
questions.explanation: And patients on statins start from a lower LDL.

summary.title: History
points: First ACL inhibitor (ETC-1002); tablets still debossed 'ESP'.
Centralised EU approval in 2020 on four 12-week LDL trials: LDL as a surrogate.
Daiichi Sankyo holds the licence; partners include Zentiva and Organon.
CLEAR Outcomes led to a CV risk-reduction indication in 2024.
Renewed November 2024 with unlimited validity; paediatric studies deferred.

exercises.scenario: A distributor asks what Nilemdo's original approval rested on.

questions.prompt: What's correct?
options: CLEAR Outcomes, which was completed before 2020
Data from the US approval only
questions.explanation: No outcome data at first.

questions.prompt: What changed in 2024?
options: A CV risk-reduction indication was added
The dose was raised to 360 mg
Children aged 4 and over were added after the paediatric plan was completed
The licence was suspended for gout
questions.explanation: Via variation II/31, based on CLEAR Outcomes.

exercises.scenario: Why do Zentiva and Organon appear in the PIL?

questions.prompt: Choose the explanation.
options: They hold their own national licences under the decentralised procedure
They own the patent in their countries
They're local partners for Daiichi Sankyo
questions.explanation: A common way to extend reach in a fragmented market.

questions.prompt: What does 'unlimited validity' after renewal mean?
options: No further five-year renewal is needed
The product can never be withdrawn, whatever new safety data appear
questions.explanation: Monitoring continues.

summary.title: What it's approved for
points: Adults only, as an adjunct to diet; primary hypercholesterolaemia (incl. HeFH) or mixed dyslipidaemia.
Nilemdo: after the maximum tolerated statin, or without a statin if intolerant or contraindicated.
Nustendi: after statin plus ezetimibe, or ezetimibe alone; or replacing the two tablets.
CV indication since 2024, tied to LDL lowering; secondary and primary prevention.
Nustendi's label admits primary-prevention evidence covers lipids only.

exercises.scenario: A statin-intolerant patient hasn't tried ezetimibe yet.

questions.prompt: Which product fits the label wording?
options: A statin at a lower dose, as the only route
Nustendi, straight away as the first step
Neither, until ezetimibe has been tried for a year
questions.explanation: Nustendi comes after ezetimibe alone isn't enough.

questions.prompt: Later she's on Nilemdo plus ezetimibe as two tablets. Can she switch to Nustendi?
options: No: Nustendi is only for patients on a statin
Only after a new LDL trial in her group
No: switching requires a washout period
Yes, as a replacement for the two tablets
questions.explanation: Substitution is one of Nustendi's routes.

exercises.scenario: A medical team wants to promote Nustendi for primary prevention of heart attacks.

questions.prompt: What does the Nustendi SmPC say?
options: Evidence in high-risk patients covers only lipid effects
CLEAR Outcomes proved a 30% benefit in primary prevention, which the label states
questions.explanation: The ezetimibe subgroup HR was 0.94 (0.74–1.20).

questions.prompt: Which group isn't in either wording?
questions.explanation: Children aren't covered either.

summary.title: Strengths and products
points: Nilemdo 180 mg: white, '180'/'ESP'; Nustendi 180/10 mg: blue, '818'/'ESP'.
Both contain lactose; Nustendi must be kept in the original pack (moisture).
MAH Daiichi Sankyo Europe; Zentiva and Organon are local representatives in some countries.
Nustendi was authorised five days before Nilemdo (27 March vs 1 April 2020).
One Nustendi tablet behaves like two separate tablets.

exercises.scenario: A pharmacy repacks Nustendi into a pill organiser.

questions.prompt: What's the problem?
options: It must be refrigerated once removed from the blister and used within a week
It must stay in the original pack, away from moisture
It loses its ezetimibe content in light
Nothing, since it needs no special storage
questions.explanation: Its blisters include an extra moisture barrier.

questions.prompt: A Nordic patient on Nustendi needs the local contact. Who?
options: Organon, as for Nilemdo in the Nordics
Zentiva, as in the Baltic states
questions.explanation: The Nordic split differs by product.

exercises.scenario: Why can Nustendi replace two separate tablets?

questions.prompt: What did the SmPC show?
options: It was tested in an outcome trial
questions.explanation: Ezetimibe peaks were 13% lower, judged not clinically significant.

questions.prompt: Which product was authorised first?
questions.explanation: Same CHMP opinion date, five days apart.

summary.title: How it's taken
points: One tablet a day, with or without food, swallowed whole.
Simvastatin: 20 mg normally, 40 mg in severe high-risk cases, above 40 mg contraindicated.
Nustendi: 2 h before or 4 h after a bile acid sequestrant; not recommended in moderate or severe liver impairment.
Missed dose: same day, take it; next day, skip it.
Contraindicated in pregnancy; SmPC allows breastfeeding to be considered, unlike older EMA overviews.

exercises.scenario: A patient takes simvastatin 80 mg and needs more LDL lowering.

questions.prompt: Can Nilemdo be added?
options: Yes, without any change to simvastatin
Yes, if CK is checked weekly
questions.explanation: Above 40 mg is contraindicated; reduce (normally 20 mg) or switch statin.

questions.prompt: She also takes cholestyramine and wants Nustendi.
options: Take Nustendi 2 h before or 4 h after it
questions.explanation: Cholestyramine cuts ezetimibe by about 55%.

exercises.scenario: A patient with Child-Pugh B liver impairment needs further LDL lowering.

questions.prompt: What do the labels say?
options: Both are fine without any dose change, since the liver isn't involved
Nilemdo is fine; Nustendi isn't recommended
questions.explanation: Ezetimibe exposure rises about fourfold in moderate impairment.

questions.prompt: A breastfeeding mother asks about bempedoic acid. Which source wins?
options: The EMA overview: must not be used while breastfeeding
The SmPC: breastfeeding may be considered
questions.explanation: Relative infant dose about 0.5%; the overviews look outdated.

summary.title: Reading a clinical trial
points: LDL effect = placebo-corrected difference (Harmony: −16.5% vs +1.6%, about 18 points).
2:1 randomisation gives more safety data, but a smaller, noisier placebo group.
'Statin-intolerant' and 'maximum tolerated' had different operational definitions per trial.
CLEAR Combo's SmPC figures come from a sensitivity analysis excluding three sites.
CLEAR Outcomes was event-driven; check which components drive MACE-4.

exercises.scenario: CLEAR Outcomes' ezetimibe subgroup: HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.74–1.20).

questions.prompt: What can you say?
options: Compatible with benefit or no effect
Proven benefit in ezetimibe users, because it's prespecified
questions.explanation: 'Consistent with the overall result' isn't 'proven in this subgroup'.

questions.prompt: Why does a 2:1 ratio matter for reading the result?
options: The placebo arm is smaller and less precise
The drug arm becomes less reliable because it is larger
questions.explanation: Combo's placebo arm had only 41 patients.

exercises.scenario: A slide says 'proven in statin-intolerant patients' without saying what that meant.

questions.prompt: Why does the definition matter?
options: It ranged from no statin to very low doses
It always meant no statin at all for at least a full year
It was identical in every trial
questions.explanation: Tranquility, Serenity and Outcomes each defined it differently.

questions.prompt: What made CLEAR Combo's result unusual?
options: It had no placebo arm, only active comparators
Three sites were dropped for non-compliance
questions.explanation: The SmPC states the reason openly.

summary.title: The pivotal trials
points: On a statin: Harmony and Wisdom, about 17–18 points LDL vs placebo.
Statin-intolerant: Serenity about 21 points; Tranquility on ezetimibe about 28.5.
Combo: Nustendi −36%, roughly the sum of its parts; 38 points vs placebo.
Outcomes: 13,970 statin-intolerant, MACE-4 HR 0.87; heart attacks and procedures fell.
Different trials and baselines: a range, not a ranking.

exercises.scenario: A partner claims 'bempedoic acid lowers LDL by 28%'.

questions.prompt: What's the fair correction?
options: That's on ezetimibe in statin-intolerant patients
That's the figure on top of maximum tolerated statins in Harmony
questions.explanation: On a statin it's about 17–18 points.

questions.prompt: Which trial is the main safety source on a statin background?
questions.explanation: Largest LDL trial, a full year.

exercises.scenario: Why is the LDL effect smaller in Harmony than in Serenity?

questions.prompt: Choose the best answer.
options: Harmony used a lower dose of 90 mg instead of 180 mg
Bempedoic acid doesn't work with statins
Statin background and lower starting LDL
questions.explanation: Different designs too, so not head-to-head.

questions.prompt: Where is the only direct comparison of the parts?
questions.explanation: All arms randomised in one trial.

summary.title: Combination trials
points: Licences: statin; 'other lipid-lowering therapies'; ezetimibe (Nustendi). PCSK9 not named.
SmPC lines: statins raised (simvastatin capped); ezetimibe ×1.6, not meaningful; fimasartan; no SGLT2/GLP-1 lines.
With evolocumab: one phase 2 trial, LDL −30% more at 2 months.
Triple PCSK9 + ezetimibe trial under way; triple FDC with atorvastatin only in a press release.
BP, SGLT2 and GLP-1 columns are empty; closest is the CLEAR Outcomes diabetes analysis.

exercises.scenario: A partner wants to market bempedoic acid on top of PCSK9 inhibitors.

questions.prompt: What's the evidence?
options: A large outcome trial with evolocumab
An EU licence naming PCSK9 inhibitors
CLEAR Harmony, which included PCSK9 users
questions.explanation: Harmony excluded PCSK9 users.

questions.prompt: A 64% LDL fall for a triple tablet comes from where?
questions.explanation: No EU triple tablet exists.

exercises.scenario: What can you say about bempedoic acid with an SGLT2 inhibitor?

questions.prompt: Choose the accurate statement.
options: Nustendi's label covers it under 'other lipid-lowering therapies'
No dedicated trial or SmPC line exists
questions.explanation: The closest evidence is the diabetes analysis, not a combination trial.

questions.prompt: What did CLEAR Outcomes show in people with diabetes?
options: Benefit held, and no more new diabetes
More new diabetes, as with statins, but benefit held overall
questions.explanation: HR 0.83; new diabetes 11.1% vs 11.5%.

summary.title: Heart-attack and stroke outcomes
points: Non-fatal MI HR 0.73; revascularisation HR 0.81.
Stroke and CV death unchanged; no significant effect on death from any cause.
NNT about 63 over about 40 months for MACE-4.
The effect size fits the LDL hypothesis (about 17% predicted vs 13% seen).
Primary-prevention subgroup figures are hypotheses; the SmPC doesn't report them.

exercises.scenario: A primary-prevention analysis reports 39% fewer CV deaths.

questions.prompt: How should you weigh it?
options: As proof of fewer CV deaths
As the basis of the EU indication
questions.explanation: The full trial showed no effect on CV death.

questions.prompt: What's the NNT for MACE-4?

exercises.scenario: Does CLEAR Outcomes fit the LDL hypothesis?

questions.prompt: What's the check?
options: LDL didn't fall in the trial
0.76 mmol/L lower predicts about 17%; 13% was seen
The hypothesis doesn't apply to non-statins
It predicts about 50%, so the result disagrees with the hypothesis
questions.explanation: Same range: consistent with benefit through LDL.

questions.prompt: Which outcome is NOT shown?
questions.explanation: Stroke HR 0.82–0.85, not significant.

summary.title: Side effects
points: Common: anaemia, gout and raised uric acid, raised AST, limb pain, lower eGFR.
Uric acid up about 48 µmol/L within 4 weeks; stop if gout symptoms appear.
Haemoglobin dips and anaemia, more with fibrates; reversible.
Creatinine up 4–6 µmol/L via OAT2, not kidney damage.
Gallstones (2.2% vs 1.2%) and tendon rupture aren't in the EU labels.

exercises.scenario: A patient with prior gout develops a hot, swollen big toe on bempedoic acid.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC say?
options: Stop if raised uric acid comes with gout symptoms
Continue; gout is unrelated to bempedoic acid in this patient
questions.explanation: Most gout cases were in people with prior gout or high uric acid.

questions.prompt: His eGFR dropped slightly. How to read it?
options: Kidney damage that needs bempedoic acid stopped urgently
questions.explanation: Interpret eGFR with care.

exercises.scenario: A safety reviewer compares CLEAR Outcomes with the label.

questions.prompt: Which finding isn't in the Nilemdo table?
options: Raised AST above three times the upper limit
questions.explanation: 2.2% vs 1.2%; Nustendi lists it only via ezetimibe.

questions.prompt: What happens to uric acid with a fibrate too?
options: Gout roughly doubles, while uric acid itself stays the same
Raised uric acid is more frequent, but not gout

summary.title: Who shouldn't take it, and interactions
points: Contraindicated: allergy, pregnancy, simvastatin above 40 mg; Nustendi with a statin in active liver disease.
Care: gout, severe kidney impairment, liver; lactose.
Statins: stop both if CPK above 10× ULN. Fibrates: TG may rise and HDL fall; check at 4 weeks.
OATP substrates (bosentan, fimasartan, some hepatitis C drugs) may rise.
Nustendi's ezetimibe: ciclosporin, cholestyramine, INR and gallstone rules.

exercises.scenario: A patient on fenofibrate starts Nilemdo.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC ask for?
options: Check TG and HDL at 4 weeks and periodically
Stop fenofibrate first, then start Nilemdo a week later
questions.explanation: The fibrate paradox.

questions.prompt: A transplant patient on ciclosporin is offered Nustendi.
options: Use Nilemdo plus extra ciclosporin to offset the interaction
Start with caution and monitor ciclosporin
questions.explanation: Ezetimibe exposure rises about 3.4×, up to 12×.

exercises.scenario: A patient on warfarin switches from Nilemdo to Nustendi.

questions.prompt: What changes?
questions.explanation: Reports of raised INR with ezetimibe.

questions.prompt: Which is a contraindication for both products?
questions.explanation: Women who could become pregnant need effective contraception.

summary.title: Pharmacovigilance
points: One PSUSA covers both products; data to Feb 2024 ended in maintenance.
After CLEAR Outcomes, myopathy with statins and gout were removed as important potential risks.
Gout remains a warning in the SmPC.
Renewed in 2024 with unlimited validity.
Watchlist: gallstones, tendon rupture, fibrate combinations.

exercises.scenario: A partner reads 'gout removed from the RMP' as 'no gout risk'.

questions.prompt: What does it really mean?
options: Bempedoic acid no longer causes gout after CLEAR Outcomes
Gout stays a warning, managed routinely
questions.explanation: It no longer needs special tracking.

questions.prompt: What was the PSUSA outcome?
options: A new gallstone warning added to both labels
questions.explanation: October 2024.

exercises.scenario: What would most likely trigger the next safety change?

questions.prompt: Choose the most plausible item.
options: A partner change in France, from Organon to Zentiva
questions.explanation: Gallstones are on the watchlist.

questions.prompt: Why is tendon rupture on the watchlist?
options: It's a labelled EU side effect for both Nilemdo and Nustendi
Raised earlier and in the US label; not increased in CLEAR Outcomes
questions.explanation: Not in either EU SmPC.

summary.title: ESC guidelines
points: 2019 guidelines predate approval: no recommendation.
2025: statin intolerance Class I (B); add-on when not at goal Class IIa (C).
Class I rests on CLEAR Outcomes; the add-on rests on LDL trials and judgement.
Label and guideline align on statin intolerance and not-at-goal.
Gap: adding to a PCSK9 inhibitor has only phase 2 evidence.

exercises.scenario: A very-high-risk patient on max statin plus ezetimibe isn't at goal.

questions.prompt: What does ESC 2025 say about adding bempedoic acid?
options: Recommended (I, A), on the basis of CLEAR Outcomes
questions.explanation: Outcome evidence was in statin-intolerant patients.

questions.prompt: Which label route fits?
options: Nustendi or Nilemdo on top of the statin
Nustendi only, and only without a statin in the regimen
questions.explanation: Nustendi after statin plus ezetimibe.

exercises.scenario: Why is statin intolerance Class I but add-on only IIa?

questions.prompt: Choose the reason.
options: Bempedoic acid doesn't lower LDL further when added to statins
The outcome trial enrolled statin-intolerant patients
questions.explanation: Add-on evidence rests on LDL trials.

questions.prompt: Which agent sits alongside it at Class I in intolerance?
questions.explanation: Ezetimibe Class I (A).

summary.title: The medicine and its story
points: An upstream LDL-lowerer for people who can't use, or aren't at goal on, statins.
Transporters explain statin interactions, creatinine and uric acid.
Approved on LDL in 2020; outcome indication in 2024; unlimited renewal.
Partners extend reach across Europe.

exercises.scenario: An investor asks what made bempedoic acid's 2024 label stronger.

questions.prompt: What's the answer?
options: CLEAR Outcomes added an outcome claim
A new formulation with better absorption
questions.explanation: Not just LDL anymore.

questions.prompt: Which mechanism explains three different label items?
options: ACSVL1 activation in muscle, which limits statin effects
questions.explanation: Statin levels, creatinine and uric acid.

questions.prompt: Why isn't there a muscle claim despite ACSVL1 being in the liver?
questions.explanation: Don't overread the mechanism.

exercises.scenario: Link history to positioning.

questions.prompt: Who was bempedoic acid aimed at?
questions.explanation: It arrived after statins, ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors.

questions.prompt: What does LDL as a surrogate mean for the 2020 approval?
options: Approval after CLEAR Outcomes had been completed
questions.explanation: Outcomes came in 2023–2024.

questions.prompt: In your own words: why do creatinine and uric acid rise, and why isn't that kidney damage?
questions.modelAnswer: Bempedoic acid blocks OAT2, a kidney transporter that helps secrete creatinine and uric acid into the urine. Less secretion means slightly higher blood levels, but filtration itself isn't worse, so the creatinine rise doesn't reflect kidney damage. eGFR estimates need careful interpretation.

summary.title: The label in practice
points: Nilemdo after a statin, or without one; Nustendi after ezetimibe, or as replacement.
CV indication since 2024; primary-prevention outcome evidence thin for Nustendi.
Simvastatin cap; bile acid sequestrant timing; Nustendi not in moderate liver impairment.
Pregnancy contraindicated; breastfeeding may be considered per SmPC.

exercises.scenario: A 58-year-old woman, statin-intolerant, on ezetimibe, LDL not at goal, Child-Pugh A.

questions.prompt: Which product fits?
questions.explanation: Not at goal on ezetimibe alone.

questions.prompt: She could become pregnant. What's needed?
questions.explanation: Contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.prompt: She has a week of vomiting. What does the PIL advise about the pill?
options: Use a backup method for 7 days
Stop Nustendi until the vomiting settles, then restart
questions.explanation: Vomiting more than 2 days may stop the pill working.

exercises.scenario: A pharmacist checks a prescription: Nustendi + simvastatin 40 mg + cholestyramine.

questions.prompt: Is simvastatin 40 mg allowed?
options: Always, as long as CK is checked every month
questions.explanation: Normally 20 mg; above 40 mg contraindicated.

questions.prompt: How should the doses be timed?
options: Nustendi 2 h before or 4 h after cholestyramine
Cholestyramine first, then Nustendi 1 h later
questions.explanation: Cholestyramine binds ezetimibe.

questions.prompt: If her liver disease progresses to Child-Pugh B?
options: Switch statin and continue Nustendi at the same dose
questions.explanation: Ezetimibe exposure rises fourfold.

summary.title: The evidence
points: LDL effects vary by background: 17–18 points on statins, 21–28 without, 38 with Nustendi.
Definitions of intolerance and 'maximum tolerated' vary; Combo used a sensitivity analysis.
CLEAR Outcomes: fewer heart attacks and procedures; not stroke or death.
Combinations beyond ezetimibe and statins have little or no evidence.

exercises.scenario: A competitor says 'bempedoic acid cuts cardiovascular deaths'.

questions.prompt: What did CLEAR Outcomes show?
options: A 39% reduction in CV deaths across the whole trial
questions.explanation: The 39% is a primary-prevention subgroup figure.

questions.prompt: What did fall?
options: Deaths from any cause, by about 13%

questions.prompt: Why can't Nustendi's −36% be directly compared with Harmony's −16.5%?
options: Nustendi contains twice the bempedoic acid dose
questions.explanation: Only within Combo are the parts compared.

exercises.scenario: A partner plans bempedoic acid + semaglutide co-promotion with an outcome claim.

questions.prompt: What supports the claim?
questions.explanation: Only the CLEAR Outcomes diabetes analysis.

questions.prompt: What did the diabetes analysis show?
options: Benefit held; no excess new diabetes
More new diabetes, offsetting the benefit
questions.explanation: HR 0.83; interaction p = 0.42.

questions.prompt: In your own words: why is the ezetimibe subgroup HR of 0.94 (0.74–1.20) not proof of benefit?
questions.modelAnswer: The interval runs from a 26% reduction to a 20% increase, so it includes no effect. The result is consistent with the overall trial but isn't precise enough to show benefit on its own in that subgroup.

summary.title: Safety and guidelines
points: Gout, anaemia, liver enzymes and OAT2 creatinine rises; gallstones on the watchlist.
Contraindications: allergy, pregnancy, simvastatin above 40 mg.
Fibrate paradox; Nustendi adds ezetimibe's interaction rules.
PSUSA maintenance; RMP slimmed; ESC Class I in intolerance, IIa as add-on.

exercises.scenario: A statin-intolerant man with prior gout, on fenofibrate and warfarin, needs LDL lowering.

questions.prompt: What's the first caution?
questions.explanation: Stop if gout symptoms appear.

questions.prompt: What monitoring does fenofibrate add?
options: CK weekly for the first three months
questions.explanation: The fibrate paradox; anaemia and uric acid too.

questions.prompt: If Nustendi is chosen, what about warfarin?
questions.explanation: Ezetimibe reports of raised INR.

exercises.scenario: How did CLEAR Outcomes change both the risk plan and the guideline?

questions.prompt: Risk plan?
options: Gout and myopathy dropped as important potential risks
A new gallstone risk was added
Gout became an identified risk needing extra studies

questions.prompt: Guideline?
options: Class IIb as an add-on only, with no intolerance role
questions.explanation: ESC 2025 focused update.

questions.prompt: Which watchlist item has trial data but no EU label line?

summary.title: Bempedoic acid: the whole picture
points: An upstream, liver-activated LDL-lowerer for patients who can't use or aren't at goal on statins.
Nilemdo after a statin; Nustendi after ezetimibe or as a replacement.
LDL −17 to −38 points depending on background; CLEAR Outcomes HR 0.87, via heart attacks and procedures.
Transporter effects: statin levels, creatinine, uric acid.
Safety: gout, anaemia, liver enzymes; gallstones on the watchlist.
ESC 2025: Class I in intolerance, IIa as add-on.

exercises.scenario: You're evaluating an in-licensing of bempedoic acid for a non-EU market.

questions.prompt: Which claim is best supported?
options: Fewer heart attacks in statin-intolerant patients
Proven benefit on top of PCSK9 inhibitors in phase 3
questions.explanation: CLEAR Outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which interaction must be in the label?
questions.explanation: Simvastatin acid doubles.

questions.prompt: Which product suits patients already on ezetimibe?
questions.explanation: Or as replacement for two tablets.

exercises.scenario: A patient story: 66, statin-intolerant, prior MI, gout history, on ezetimibe, LDL 2.9 mmol/L.

questions.prompt: Which route fits?
options: A high-dose statin, since intolerance usually passes
questions.explanation: CV indication covers established disease.

questions.prompt: What should be watched first?
questions.explanation: Most gout in CLEAR Outcomes was in people with prior gout.

questions.prompt: What does ESC 2025 say for him?
options: Class IIb, may be considered only
questions.explanation: Alongside ezetimibe Class I (A).
